original.target_description: Huang (2014), Study 1: cleanliness versus neutral priming comparison of the composite moral judgment rating averaged across six vignettes, within the naturally occurring low response effort subsample defined by below-median survey duration.

n.sample_role: Participants in the final low response effort subsample used in the independent-samples comparison of composite moral judgments.
n.exclusions: Study 1 retained 214 of 268 recruited participants after planned exclusions for hypothesis guessing or insufficient effort responding on moral judgment items. The planned exclusion section reports 2 hypothesis guessers and 54 respondents faster than 675 words/minute on at least two moral vignettes; these counts are not summed because overlap is not specified. The critical subsample comprises retained participants below the median survey duration. End-of-survey quality-control/IER scale exclusions were supplementary, not the primary analysis.
n.location: Study 1, Results, paragraph following Table 1; Table 1, Identified low response effort subsample

notes: Identity verified from supplied canonical text: title exactly matches the neutral Huang reference; author Jason L. Huang; DOI 10.3389/fpsyg.2014.01276; marked ORIGINAL RESEARCH article, published 06 November 2014 in Frontiers in Psychology. This is a substantive full primary article web parse containing Study 1 methods, results, Table 1, Study 2, discussion and references, not an abstract-only excerpt. No PDF supplied. Only n_o was assigned; all other statistic fields, replication side and reported_success are unassigned placeholders. Target identified by Study 1 and the six-vignette composite comparison within the measured low response effort group, not by numeric matching. The Results paragraph explicitly prints n = 107 and immediately describes the composite comparison in this subsample. Table 1 independently gives mutually exclusive cleanliness n = 50 and neutral n = 57; 50 + 57 = 107 corroborates the directly printed N, but N was not inferred from df or recruitment totals. No effect-size conversion performed.
